summary: Cook County, MN: a 1922-23 steel tower on Cascade Peak and a 1933 Trout Lake tower share the name; the Forest Fire Lookout Association lists its Cascade point as gone, with no removal date found.

facts.design: Steel tower about 80 feet tall (first Cascade, 1922); the county survey calls it a ladder tower with a square cab, while Bachman describes three posts and an open crow's nest
facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists its Cascade point (the 1933 tower's location) as gone; Central US Lookouts ends with the word 'Removed' but gives no date; no removal date or description of either site today was found

staffing.status: Staffed in 1922 (probably): a John Metcalf of the Forestry Department was reported staying at the lookout in July 1922, not confirmed as the clerk; no later staffing in sources read

facts.agency: Built by the Minnesota Forest Service; Superior National Forest per Central US Lookouts

events.note: First Cascade erected on Cascade Peak, reported June 1922; the county survey dates it 1923
A John Metcalf of the Forestry Department, not confirmed as the clerk, was reported staying at the lookout in July 1922
Second Cascade, also called New Cascade or Trout Lake lookout; 100-foot ladder tower on a hill near Trout Lake

corrections.current: 47.73236, -90.58662 (FFLA point) as the single location for Cascade Lookout Tower
corrections.proposed: Keep this point for the 1933 Trout Lake tower; give the 1922-23 Cascade Peak tower its own record at 47.7511, -90.5347 (county survey)
corrections.why: The FFLA point matches the 1933 tower in the state list; the county survey places the first Cascade at a different point, so one record currently describes two towers

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The June 1922 newspaper reports the tower raised that month; the county survey gives 1923. The story uses 1922 and notes the survey date.
The county survey calls the first Cascade a ladder tower with a square cab; Bachman, quoted in the state list, describes a three-post tower with an open crow's nest. Both are reported.
The FFLA point matches the 1933 tower; the county survey places the first tower at 47.7511, -90.5347; Wikidata gives a third point. The map pin may belong to either tower.
The county survey lists the owner of the first tower as the Minnesota Forest Service; the Central US Lookouts page header names the Superior National Forest. Both are reported.

notes_for_editor: Two towers share the name Cascade: the 1922-23 tower on Cascade Peak and the 1933 New Cascade or Trout Lake tower. The record's FFLA point matches the 1933 tower; the 1922 tower is at 47.7511, -90.5347 per the county survey. Height is left out because the two towers differ (about 80 ft first, 100 ft second). No removal date found for either tower. The Wikidata photo dated 1925 is not clearly tied to either tower. Access unknown.
